what: Exploratory analyses E1 to E5 of the v3 scored run of score/PREREG.md v3.2 (fiber_strip_small_v1 off Paris 4). Units: sv = level-2 voxels = 9.596 um. Every number in this file is exploratory, not pre-registered; the pre-registered results are the three reports, unchanged.

checks.note: do the re-implementations reproduce the reports and plans? report_* and plan_* values are quoted unchanged from the pre-registered reports and frozen plans for comparison

E1_per_fiber.method: per fiber: mean |d| = sum(strip_nodes * strip_mean_abs_sv) / sum(strip_nodes) over the fiber's strips (per_strip); this equals the fiber's pooled mean over its covered nodes, because per_strip counts and averages exactly the covered nodes of the scored rows. Fiber floor: fiber_floor_mean_abs_sv weighted the same way by strip_nodes (node-weighted, as asked); per_strip has no count of floor rows, so for the fibers with two strips this is a node-, not row-, weighted mean of the two strips' floors (the report pools the floor over rows: one point per scored row). Summary statistics give each fiber equal weight.

E2_weighting.note: PREREG 5.3 ("pooled over nodes") and 6 (G2: "a pooled mean |d| of at most 1.5 sv; at least 70 % of nodes within 2 sv") make the pre-registered gate node-weighted: nodes are pooled over all scored fibers, the fiber is only the bootstrap cluster (5.4). The re-weightings below are descriptive only; they are not a gate and change neither the G2 verdict ("secondary: transfers") nor any pre-registered number.

end_proximity.rule_of_thumb: on a fiber end that is a true end, the strip keeps no row within 75 sv of it; a crossing closer than about 45 sv to it has no strip node within 30 sv on that side (straight fiber), and one closer than 105 sv has fewer

missing_crossings.method: The scorer's crossing rule (score_strips.crossing_agreement) re-run in numpy on the 25 strips and the 24 fibers of the 15 run crossings: every strip associated with its nearest fiber (median row centre distance <= 5 sv); per fiber, the strip with the most valid nodes within 30 sv of the crossing point (near_strip; none if no node); each direction needs >= 5 such nodes and >= 5 of them covered by the other strip (projection port of GridSurface.project). Separately, PREREG 7's text rule evaluated on the strips of the pieces that hold the crossing's two windows, both directions always tried. Row classes from strip.npz: a row with stitch weight > 0 that is invalid and lies within 75 sv of the piece start, or after the last valid row, was removed by infer.py's end trim (rows of piece arclength < 75 sv or > L - 75 sv, L the piece's kink-repaired length).

piece.note: the piece starts at line index 150 of the JSON, the first point of the fiber's controlled span (the line_offset of the plan's fiber record): the start of the fiber in the full AFV too, so a full infer_all run starts there as well (first head k = 0 at 24 sv)

P0005.explanation: P0005 holds one stretch, S0026, at fiber arclength 0.0 to 43.0 sv: it starts at the first sample of the fiber's controlled span (the fiber is 7667.8 sv long). The piece starts there too (fiber s 0.0 to 232.2 sv), so its start is a true fiber end. Its 4 decisions (heads 24 to 72 sv) give rows from -6.5 to 101.5 sv of the piece; infer.py's 75 sv end trim removes every row below 75 sv (21 rows with decisions, piece arclength [-6.5, 73.5]), which includes all 11 rows lying in the stretch. The 7 rows left (175 nodes, piece arclength [77.5, 101.5]) lie at fiber arclength 77 to 102 sv, beyond the stretch's end at 43 sv, so the scorer finds no row inside it. The mask is not the cause: mask.tif equals the x/y/z validity and no row is partly valid. PREREG 4.6 says the trim reaches a scored row only at a true fiber end, where a full run trims the same way: this is that case (a full run would also leave this stretch without a row). The fiber is still scored through P0006 (31 stretches), so no fiber was lost.

end_trim_in_the_plans.note: raw JSON arclength; infer.py trims in the piece's kink-repaired arclength, which is shorter by the repairs inside the piece (before the first head by up to 20.9 sv, piece C0007; per plan in kink_repair_offset_at_first_head), so the overlaps and distances are approximate. "distance" is from a window to the cut piece end; "margin beyond the trim zone" subtracts the 75 sv trim. A window reaching a trim zone loses its rows there (whole rows). scored_in_report: the stretch is in a per_strip entry (secondary, primary), or the crossing has a value (PHerc0332).
